messages.subject: Caching with reactive expressions
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to use reactive expressions in a way to cache the output on
first run for future calls. My code:

#functions.R:
runQuery <- function(dimension) {
#Stuff

return(result)
}


#server.R:
source("functions.R", local=TRUE)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
getData <- reactive({
runQuery(input$dimension)
})

output$plot <- renderPlot({
data <- getData()

#ggplot2 stuff
})
})


#ui.R:
<select id="dimension">
<option value="foo.bar" selected="selected">foo.bar</option>
<option value="baz.bbq">baz.bbq</option>
</select>



When a selection (a dimension value) is made from the UI, runQuery()
incorporates the value in its query and returns a response which is used
to plot.

What I'm experiencing is that a previously selected action is
re-executing runQuery(). My expectation was that a query which was
previously executed would have been cached given that the
input$dimension value is the same and thus preventing the trip to
runQuery() on subsequent actions.

If anyone can shed some light on this, it'd be greatly appreciated.

Thanks,

-Sarven
http://csarven.ca/#i

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: Caching with reactive expressions
parts:
Hi Sarven -

Reactive expressions will only cache the most recent values -- this is so that if you have multiple outputs (or reactive expressions) that uses getData(), it won't have to run again. However, it doesn't cache old values from previous runs. If you want to do that, you'll have to cache values yourself.


You could use the memoise package to do caching. When you pass memoise() a function, it will return another function that caches return values, based in the input.

# Create a memoized version of runif()
rr <- memoise(runif)

# First run, with input 1
rr(1)
# [1] 0.6785051

# All subsequent runs with the same input (1) return the same value, because
# it is cached
rr(1)
# [1] 0.6785051

# Input of 2 will run runif(2)
rr(2)
[1] 0.5760216 0.7925082
rr(1)
# [1] 0.6785051



Keep in mind, though, that if you use memoise, the scope where you define the memoized function matters. To use it in a Shiny app so that each session gets its own cache, define it within the shinyServer function:

shinyServer(function (input, output) {
  # Create memoized function in scope of each session
  rr <- memoise(runif)

  output$numbers <- renderText({
    rr(input$n)
  })
})



If you want it to be shared across all sessions, define it outside the shinyServer function:

# Create memoized function in scope shared across all sessions
rr <- memoise(runif)

shinyServer(function (input, output) {
  output$numbers <- renderText({
    rr(input$n)
  })
})



-Winston

Hi Winston,

This is excellent! Thank you for that pointer.

I think building on top of this, or perhaps a better way would be to
actually cache the results to disk and then reuse when possible, since
restarting the server would clear cache.

-Sarven
